description: A treasury director must authorize a special dividend from a profitable subsidiary and finalize the dividend amount, payment date, solvency documentation, and withholding-tax process, with input from liquidity planning, legal, and tax.

shared_context.S1: Northstar Components has $8,600,000 of cash available for distribution after its ordinary operating payments.
shared_context.S2: The parent company has requested a special dividend from Northstar Components before the end of the third quarter.
shared_context.S3: The draft request proposes a $4,000,000 dividend with no finalized payment date or supporting process terms.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final authorization decision.
shared_context.S5: As part of the normal treasury approval routine, Mara obtains a review from liquidity planning, legal, and tax before signing the distribution instruction.

PF1.text: Elias completed the subsidiary's cash forecast this morning and confirmed that the largest authorized dividend payment preserving the required $5,000,000 post-distribution operating reserve is exactly $3,600,000; the dividend amount is the gross authorized dividend before any withholding is remitted, and the forecast supports paying it on September 30, 2026. The updated forecast has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Nadia found in the subsidiary's articles while reviewing the corporate file this week that any distribution above $3,000,000 requires a signed solvency certificate from two directors before payment; this requirement is not yet on the transaction checklist.

PF3.text: Victor confirmed in a tax memo received this morning that the dividend requires a 5% withholding reserve and that the withheld amount must be remitted within 10 business days after payment; the memo has not yet been attached to the distribution file.

acceptance_conditions: The dividend must be approved for exactly $3,600,000.
The subsidiary must retain exactly $5,000,000 as its post-distribution operating reserve.
The payment date must be September 30, 2026.
A solvency certificate signed by two directors must be required before payment.
A 5% withholding reserve must be established.
The withheld tax must be remitted within 10 business days after payment.
The settlement must include commitments for the director solvency certificate and withholding-tax remittance.

content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] in ['Nadia', 'Legal'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] in ['Victor', 'Tax'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft requests $4,000,000 without a verified reserve calculation, while PF1 changes the authorized gross dividend amount to exactly $3,600,000, the retained reserve to exactly $5,000,000, and the payment date to September 30, 2026.
The draft contains no special legal closing condition, while PF2 changes the settlement to require a solvency certificate signed by two directors before payment.

The draft has no tax process, while PF3 changes the required withholding reserve to exactly 5%, sets tax remittance at exactly 10 business days after payment, and requires a withholding-tax remittance commitment.
